title: Integrated Security & Compliance Guidance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows
author: Maya Kapoor
body:
Executive summary:
This document provides a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls covering RBAC and authentication, audit logging and retention, data residency and retention requirements, secure SDLC gates, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exception handling. It is intended for security engineers, platform engineers, SREs, product owners, and compliance stakeholders.

1) Scope and audience
- Applies to Redwood-managed control plane components, hosted services, Dedicated and Private deployment support artifacts, and operational tooling that process production or regulated customer data.
- Excludes ephemeral developer-only environments that never touch production data.
- Primary audience: security, eng-infra, eng-sre, eng-platform, compliance, and engineering managers.

2) High-level principles
- Principle of least privilege: default deny; grant minimal permissions required for tasks.
- Separation of duties: critical operations require multi-person approval and are logged.
- Defense in depth: combine authentication, authorization, encryption, monitoring, and controls to reduce blast radius.
- Evidence-first: controls must produce attestable artifacts for audits and regulatory review.

3) RBAC and authentication
- Role layers: platform-level roles (console/control plane) and service-level roles (per microservice/API).
- Canonical platform roles: system-admin, security-admin, infra-operator, app-owner, viewer, support-agent.
- Identity sources: corporate SSO (OIDC/SAML) is canonical for humans; service identities use short-lived mTLS certificates and JWTs from the platform token service (default rotation: 24h).
- Policy examples: maintain machine-readable policy snippets in the policy repo; example policy names include model-metrics-viewer and deployment-admin.
- Role lifecycle: new roles require security-admin review; privileged roles undergo quarterly access certification.
- Emergency (break-glass): two-person approval, max session duration 6 hours, recorded and followed by post-use review.

4) Audit logging
- Required events: auth attempts, token issuance/revocation, role/permission changes, configuration changes, data export actions, admin API calls, and system security alerts.
- Event schema: timestamp (UTC RFC3339), actor, resource, action, request_id, trace_id, and client metadata (IP, region, client-version).
- Pipeline: application -> Audit-Collector -> Kafka audit-events -> processors -> immutable archive (WORM S3) + SIEM (Splunk/Elastic).
- Ingestion SLO: 99.9% of events delivered to SIEM within 60s.
- Integrity: daily signed cross-checksum manifests, weekly rehashing and reconciliation.
- Retention: default 13 months for operational audit logs; regulated customers may contract up to 7 years.
- Access controls: audit buckets restricted to security-admin, infra-operator, and compliance reviewers; MFA required and access logged.

5) Data residency and retention
- Classification labels: PII, Customer Confidential, Internal, Public; dataset labels maintained in the metadata catalogue.
- Regions supported: us-east-1 (NA), eu-west-1 (EU), ap-southeast-1 (APAC); residency selected at provisioning; compute and storage isolated per tenant region.
- Controls: region-locked buckets, disabled cross-region routing by default, VPC endpoints per region, DLP scans required for cross-region transfers.
- Retention summary: authentication events 13 months (default), audit archives 13 months hot / up to 7 years cold by contract, customer backups 30 days default, billing 7 years.
- Deletion proof: signed deletion manifest stored in the evidence bucket with object IDs, operator, deletion timestamp, and verification checksum.

6) Secure SDLC controls
- Required gates: SAST with PR blocking for HIGH/CRITICAL, dependency vulnerability scanning (CVSS >= 7.0 requires mitigation plan), IaC policy-as-code checks, secrets scanning, and manual security review for data-impacting features.
- Toolchain: GitHub branch protection, Dependabot, Snyk/Checkmarx, Trivy, Terrascan, CI runners owned by eng-infra.
- Release checklist: CI green, security signoff when required, SBOM generated, feature flags for staged rollout, post-deploy smoke tests, rollback playbook attached.

7) Incident response (security)
- Roles: Incident Commander, Forensics lead, Platform lead, Communications lead, Legal & Compliance.
- Severity levels: Sev-1 critical (confirmed exfiltration or prod-wide outage), Sev-2 high (subset tenant impact or suspected PII exposure), Sev-3 medium, Sev-4 low.
- Immediate containment steps: capture volatile evidence, isolate affected nodes, revoke/rotate credentials, enable elevated logging and preserve logs to WORM storage.
- Forensics: chain-of-custody documentation, approved tooling and image formats, store evidence under the incidents path in the compliance bucket with object-lock enabled.
- Notifications: follow regional regulatory timelines (e.g., GDPR 72 hours); Legal and Product are engaged immediately for Sev-1.

8) Compliance evidence workflows
- Canonical artifacts: access review snapshots, audit manifests, SAST/DAST reports, deployment manifests, policy change tickets, backup snapshots, deletion attestations.
- Naming convention: controlId_artifactType_YYYYMMDD_owner (file extension .json or .pdf).
- Collection process: identify evidence per control, trigger automated exports where available, perform manual collection with signed attestation when automation is not available, attach evidence reference to controlbook entries.
- Storage and access: evidence store s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/ with MFA delete and object-lock; access limited to Security, Compliance, and auditors and requires ticketed approval.

9) Risk and exceptions
- Exception request requires: owner, control affected, justification, compensating controls, duration, risk acceptance, mitigation plan, and expiry date.
- Submission via SEC-EXCEPTIONS board; Security performs initial triage.
- Approval: low-risk exceptions approved by Security lead; high-risk require Security + Legal + Product and executive risk acceptance signature.
- Compensating controls: increased monitoring, restricted session recording, reduced credential lifetime, network isolation. Exceptions expire automatically and owners are notified 30 days before expiry for renewal.

10) Ownership and cadence
- Document owner: Security. Other owners: Eng-infra (SDLC automation and evidence pipeline), Compliance (audit submissions), Eng-sre (operational runbooks).
- Review cadence: quarterly review and post-Sev-1 incident review; control mappings maintained in the integrated controlbook.

11) Appendix highlights and examples
- Revoke API key (CLI): curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/keys/revoke" -d '{"key_id":"abcd-1234"}'
- Export audit manifest (CLI): aws s3 cp s3://audit-manifests/daily/2026-03-03/manifest.json ./manifest.json --region us-east-1
- Retention policy example: control_id=AUD-001, retention_days=395, owner=security@redwood.example.com
- Audit pipeline diagram (text): [Application] -> Audit-Collector -> Kafka (audit-events) -> Processor -> WORM S3 + SIEM
